summary: Nora keeps one account of each person per group, written when that person has said enough rather than whenever their room is revised, and every account she writes, of a room or a person, has to point at the messages it rests on.
details: A person's account is written by its own background pass from what they said across all of the group's rooms, about every 100 messages or weekly; it is shown in that group's rooms that list them.
The pass may ask her memory about the person, but the account no longer depends on a memory answer fetched beforehand.
She also keeps an account of each group as a whole, written from her accounts of its rooms when they change, and reads it in that group's rooms after the room's own.

She also starts keeping an account of what she herself is like in each group, from how people responded to her messages there; it must rest on their responses, never on her own words alone, and nothing reads it yet.
Accounts that existed per room are not carried over, because one room's account would then be shown in every room of the group; each person's group account is written fresh shortly after start.
A refused write tells her why, so she can correct it in the same pass; a pass that settles nothing is retried rather than spent.
limitations: A citation is per account, not per sentence: the check proves an account rests on real messages, not that each line does.
No account reads presence (where people were or what they are doing now), the room's own included, because these accounts are shown in rooms whose location settings differ.
